label: third original token (s/t/u/...) after an o/m-o/m opening
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). About half the activation mass is a crisp original-phase component: step t=2 when the first two original tokens are both from {o,m} (oo, om, mo, mm) and the third token is one of s,t,u,v,i,d,g,p,1 (s and t are strongest). This predicate reaches about 83% precision on dev. It never fires at t=0, t=1, the delimiter, or original positions after 3. The other half of the mass is in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1-2 (right after <DEL>), with the input usually s/t (also g,1,b) and the upcoming outputs often z/x/digits. The top activations (up to 0.195) come from this copy component, for example the echoed first token t before z x. I could not capture that component with a token predicate: s/t-in-copy rules had under 3% precision. So the predicate covers only the original-phase part, and recall is about 43%. Magnitude is narrow (median 0.116, max 0.195).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=2 & prev_tok=o (+6.97), t=2 & prev_tok=m (+6.71), t=3 & prev_tok=o (+4.68), phase=2 & in_tok=s (+4.66), t=3 & prev_tok=m (+4.52), phase=2 & in_tok=g (+3.48). Lower it: orig0=s (-3.28), prev2_tok=x (-2.20), to_go=0 (-1.15), in_first=0 (-0.79).
